warmup.description: Activate deep core, prep bracing under load, and mobilize hips and spine.
movements: Dead bug x 10 per side (slow and controlled)
Glute bridge march x 10 per side
World’s greatest stretch x 5 per side

main_exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat (Core Emphasis)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a challenging load you could perform for 7-8 reps, leaving 1-2 reps in reserve
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep elbows high and torso upright to maximize core bracing throughout the lift.

main_exercises.name: Weighted Hanging Leg Raise
main_exercises.load_guidance: Hold a light dumbbell between feet or use ankle weights; choose a load that maintains strict control
main_exercises.form_cue: Avoid swinging and lift legs by engaging the abs, finishing with a slight pelvic curl.

main_exercises.name: Barbell Rollout (from knees or standing progression)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a range of motion that is challenging but allows you to maintain spinal neutrality
main_exercises.form_cue: Brace hard and avoid letting the lower back sag as you extend forward.

main_exercises.name: Heavy Dumbbell Suitcase Carry
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose a heavy load that significantly challenges your ability to resist leaning
main_exercises.form_cue: Stay tall and resist any lateral shift as you walk.

main_exercises.name: Decline Sit-Up with Plate Reach
main_exercises.load_guidance: Hold a moderate plate or dumbbell; select a weight that allows full range without jerking
main_exercises.form_cue: Control both the upward and downward phases, reaching slightly forward at the top.

cooldown.description: Release tension in the core and restore spinal mobility after heavy bracing work.
movements: Child’s pose x 60s with deep breathing
Supine spinal twist x 45s per side
Hip flexor stretch x 45s per side

phase_notes.menstrual: Approach this session with caution—reduce loads and consider fewer sets, especially for front squats and rollouts. Focus on maintaining good bracing rather than pushing intensity.
phase_notes.follicular: Great phase to push strength—aim to increase load slightly on front squats and carries while maintaining strong form. Take advantage of improved recovery and energy.
phase_notes.ovulatory: You may feel at your strongest—challenge yourself on compound lifts and loaded core work, but stay mindful of control and alignment during dynamic movements.
phase_notes.early_luteal: You can still train hard here, but be mindful of fatigue buildup—focus on clean reps and slightly longer rest if needed to sustain output.
phase_notes.late_luteal: This high-intensity session may feel more demanding—consider reducing load, shortening sets, or swapping to a moderate session while maintaining good movement quality.
